Let $C,e,B$ and $N$ be natural numbers, let $m$ and $s$ be Boolean flags, let $f$ map
bit strings to bit strings, and let $h$ be a bit string. Suppose $v$ assigns a natural
number to each of $14$ registers, every value $v_r$ is at most $B$, $v_3=v_0+2N$ if $s$
is true and $v_{11}=v_0+N$ if $s$ is false, $v_{13}+N\le B$, and $v_{13}\le v_5$. For
the counter program determined by these parameters, if $v_5<v_{13}+N$, there is a run
from the search state to the suffix-hit state when $s$ is true and to the prefix-hit
state when $s$ is false; at its endpoint, registers $0$ and $13$ have values
$v_0+k(v_5-v_{13})$ and $v_5$, respectively, where $k=2$ when $s$ is true and $k=1$
otherwise. If $v_5\ge v_{13}+N$, there is a run to the false-answer state when $s$ is
true and to the separator state when $s$ is false; registers $0$ and $13$ then have
values $v_3$ and $v_{13}+N$ when $s$ is true, and $v_{11}$ and $v_{13}+N$ when $s$ is
false. In either case, every configuration before the endpoint satisfies the program's
step-validity condition and has all register values at most $B$.
